public_rationale: Marcus guessed that neurosymbolic and similar alternatives got about 1% or less of total AI investment. PitchBook data reported by Bloomberg puts 2025 AI venture funding near $193 billion by September. Known neurosymbolic rounds, such as Kognitos's $25 million Series B, are small by comparison. One market-research page estimates about $340 million in neurosymbolic venture funding over 2024 and 2025, which would be well under 1%. But that source has an unknown method and apparent errors. I found no reliable dataset that tracks this category. The category itself ('alternative approaches like') is undefined, and so is 'total investments'. The order of magnitude leans his way, but no credible source measures the share, so the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: The claim is self-described as a guess.
The category and the denominator are both undefined.
No primary or independent dataset tracks neurosymbolic funding.
The 'wildly underfunded' judgement is normative and is not scored.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Neurosymbolic AI and other alternatives are wildly underfunded, receiving perhaps 1% or less of total AI investment.

statement.excerpt: Meanwhile alternative approaches like neurosymbolic AI continue to be wildly underfunded, receiving, if I had to guess maybe 1%, probably less, of total investments.
statement.document_title: AI Agents have, so far, mostly been a dud

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at the time of the post, money going to neurosymbolic AI (and similar non-LLM approaches) was about 1% or less of total AI investment.

'Total investments' is read as total AI investment. That could mean venture funding into AI or AI spending more broadly, including big-tech capex. Venture funding is the narrowest denominator, so it is the one most favourable to testing the 1% ceiling.

No period is named. It describes the state at the time of the post, so the target period is calendar 2025 up to the post date (2025-01 to 2025-08). That is the latest period funding data could report on.
'Wildly underfunded' is a value judgement and is not scored. Only the roughly-1%-or-less share is checkable.
criteria.support_condition: A credible tally of 2025 funding for neurosymbolic or other non-LLM alternative approaches shows it at about 1% or less of total AI investment for the same period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible tally shows neurosymbolic or alternative-approach funding clearly above about 1% of total AI investment in 2025, for example well over 2%.

evidence.excerpt: Venture capitalists poured US$192.7 billion into artificial intelligence start-ups so far this year
evidence.explanation: Gives the size of the denominator: AI venture funding was near $200 billion in 2025. On this base, 1% would be about $2 billion. It does not say how much went to neurosymbolic work.

evidence.excerpt: Kognitos also announced its $25 million series B funding round.
evidence.explanation: A typical 2025 round for a self-described neurosymbolic startup is in the tens of millions of dollars. That is tiny next to frontier-LLM rounds, but one deal cannot measure a sector's share.

evidence.excerpt: Venture capital investment in neuro-symbolic AI startups reached an estimated $340 million in aggregate funding rounds during 2024-2025
evidence.explanation: If accurate, this would put neurosymbolic funding far below 1% of AI venture funding. But the method is not disclosed, the report contains apparent errors, it covers two years rather than the target period, and its publication date is unclear. It cannot settle the claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A PitchBook, Crunchbase, CB Insights or Dealroom tally, or an independent study, giving 2025 funding for neurosymbolic or non-LLM AI approaches alongside total AI investment for the same period.
